irregularities.title: Root cause of DrivenData portal error 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]'
irregularities.finding: DrivenData's submission validator checks finite [0, 1] compliance across the uploaded single-band raster; GeoTIFFs encoding the 7,111,787 outside-footprint cells as IEEE-754 NaN (`-nan.tif`, e.g. `gems24-h25-1-dotted-h19-5-d1-5-20261002-989f59505db1-nan.tif` or `gems30-MSDB1-...tif`) or `-9999.0` float32 sentinels trigger `Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]` whenever NaN/nodata handling differs.
irregularities.resolution: Shipped exclusively `-zeros.tif` (`nodata=None`, all 12,279,160 pixels finite float32 in `{0.0, 1.0}`, 0 NaN inside or outside footprint, 0 Inf, 0 negative values), verified programmatically by 13/13 checks in `submission.py` and `tests/test_lwst_submission.py`. Review 2026-10-28: the shipped file passes the format gate recomputed from the raster (scripts/independent_review.py). The portal error's root cause (NaN outside the footprint) is still UNVERIFIED: no portal log was available, so this remains a hypothesis.

irregularities.title: Cross-site duplication across all 9 focus sites' Era-1 leaderboard winners (H19-5 / D2.8 family)
irregularities.finding: Every Era-1 live-scored winner across GEMSDOE24..36 (`0.2449` to `0.2778`) has 86.7%–100.0% within-3px dot overlap with the GEMSDOE32 0.2778 Champion (`e5eb6e7e-zeros.tif`). Moreover, GEMSDOE25 and GEMSDOE30 (`e56ea318af89-zeros.tif`, 0.2600) are byte-identical (`XOR = 0`), and GEMSDOE28 `h27-4` and GEMSDOE31 `h27-4` (`8acb75e1`, 0.2708) have `XOR = 0` positive pixels.
irregularities.resolution: All Era-1 files are marked DO NOT RESUBMIT in the Executive Summary table; GEMSDOESASS3 achieves 41.53% overlap vs the 0.2778 Champion and <= 63.27% across all 385 genuine rasters. CORRECTION 2026-10-28: the independent audit (evidence/independent_uniqueness_lwst_20261028.json) compared 451 submitted rasters and finds the maximum within-3 px overlap of the shipped LWST file is 66.53% (vs gemsdoe32-h49, 2026-10-27T23:50Z), not 63.27%. That is below 70% on the downloads only. The literal rule that includes the calibration lattice gives 99.78% (IR-SASS3-19).

irregularities.title: Synthetic 206,895-dot 5x5 px calibration lattice (`13gems_20261001_r13-lattice-s5_v2_nan-outside.tif`) in historical archive
irregularities.finding: Because max Euclidean distance on a 5x5 px grid is sqrt(2^2 + 2^2) = 2.828 <= 3.0 px, its 3-px buffer covers 99.871% of the entire 5,167,373-pixel footprint, causing any footprint-spanning map (including random noise and the 0.2778 Champion) to register ~99.8% raw 3-px proximity despite Spearman ~ 0.00.
irregularities.resolution: `registry_audit.py` separates synthetic space-filling calibration probes (`coverage >= 70%`) via null-calibrated excess (`passed = True`), AND GEMSDOESASS3 literally passes `< 70%` 3-px overlap (`max = 63.27%`) and `|Spearman| <= 0.90` (`max = 0.1255`) against 100% of all 378 valid rasters in the 9 focus sites and all 385 genuine rasters.

irregularities.title: Era-2 scarp-only ML off-catalogue regression in GEMSDOE36 (`KPL-36`) and GEMSDOE28 (`S22-CTXHGB`)
irregularities.finding: Both Oct 26 sibling candidates achieved high quaternary OOF (`0.1407` with non-standard 8-px collar in GEMSDOE36; `0.1449` in GEMSDOE28) by concentrating dots near visible fault tips or smooth regional elevation bands, causing off-catalogue `GEMSDOE32-SGMC-CAL-v3.0` to drop to `0.0445` (-30.7%) and `0.0505` (-21.2%) vs the 0.2778 Champion (`0.0641`).
irregularities.resolution: RETRACTED 2026-10-28: the "paired 95% CI [+0.0035, +0.0207]" compared a per-fold OOF HIDE-RECOVER value (0.111062) with a static D2.8-parent value (0.099202) that was labelled as the 0.2778 champion. The comparison is not like-for-like and must not be cited (see IR-SASS3-08). The shipped-file static HIDE-RECOVER value is 0.006130.

irregularities.title: Laplacian sign convention (`curv_s1 > 0` in V-shaped stream thalwegs) & hard PU negative screening leak
irregularities.finding: `ndimage.gaussian_laplace(dem)` is positive in concave-up drainage stream thalwegs rather than convex scarp breaks; additionally, deleting `unsup >= q97` only from `y = 0` while keeping `unsup` as a tree feature induces P(y=1 | unsup >= q97) = 1.0 in tree leaves.
irregularities.resolution: Added explicit V-shaped thalweg (`curv_s1 > 0`) and ridge-summit (`tophat >> 0`) vetoes on rectilinear planar scarps (lifting `EXP1` zero-supervision `SGMC-CAL` from `0.0480` to `0.0752`) and replaced hard `q97` negative deletion with clean 5-px collar Dual-Objective (Binary + 300 m Kernel Regressor) HGB training (lifting `EXP2` `HIDE-RECOVER` from `0.0860` to `0.1167`).

irregularities.title: Independent uniqueness audit excluded the calibration lattice; literal rule blocks the file
irregularities.finding: The 2026-10-28 downloads audit compared 451 submitted rasters and reported max within-3 px overlap 66.53%, so it reported the file as unique. The audit excluded non-download rasters, including inputs/calibration/13gems_20261001_r13-lattice-s5_v2_nan-outside.tif. Protocol Rule 1 says "any registry raster". Recomputed here: 99.7849% of the 37,654 dots lie within 3 px of the lattice (SHA-256 b4570b40... matches the pin on main; same CRS, shape and transform). This fails the 70% limit. Main's review (docs/research/review-20261028.md) reaches the same block. Coverage analysis: 99.90% of the footprint lies within 3 px of a lattice positive, leaving 5,379 footprint pixels outside the buffer. Passing at 37,654 dots needs at least 11,297 dots there, so the literal rule cannot be met at this dot count by any raster.
irregularities.resolution: Verdict corrected to NOT OK to submit under the literal rule (scripts/independent_review.py, lattice_gate). Whether the synthetic lattice should count is a protocol decision for the owner; no exemption is applied here. The owner must decide whether synthetic calibration probes count under Rule 1. Without an amendment, no file with this dot budget can pass.

irregularities.title: Shared uniqueness auditor counted non-submission feature layers as registry rasters

irregularities.resolution: FIXED in the shared tool: each raster is tagged submission / calibration / other. Protocol Rule 1 is applied to submission + calibration only. 'other' rasters are listed but not gated. Both candidates were rerun: evidence/uniqueness_scoped_lwst_20261028.json and evidence/uniqueness_scoped_sardeconf_20261028.json.
